*The skill that makes skills, and refuses to call one done until a real run is frozen.*

> **A skill is done when a real run of it is frozen in its evals — not when the files exist.**

## Why install this

Every skill in this repo carries the same freight: press branding, a
ghfactory-verified CI caller, a marketplace entry, a required check, a
`skill-invariants.json`, a baseline eval. `CLAUDE.md` documents adding one as a
**ten-step manual checklist**, and every step of it is invisible when skipped.
`ci / shipflow` gated nothing on `main` from the day it was introduced, because
one of those steps was done by hand and half-done.

skillfactory applies the ten steps as one all-or-nothing command, and spends the saved
attention on the part that decides whether a skill is any good: its one rule, the
line between what code decides and what the model decides, and a real run frozen
as its baseline.

The scaffolded baseline test **fails** until that run happens, so `ci / <name>`
cannot go green on a skill nobody has run. Rung 3 is structural, not a promise.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/skillfactory/SKILL.md` | The ladder, the flow, and the model gate. |
| `skills/skillfactory/scripts/skillfactory.js` | The CLI: `detect`, `spec`, `check-spec`, `scaffold`, `freeze`, `verify`. |
| `skills/skillfactory/scripts/lib/` | The registries, the two-tier conformance list, the scaffold plan, the README contract. |
| `skills/skillfactory/references/anatomy.md` | The fixed shape of a generated skill. |
| `skills/skillfactory/references/wiring.md` | The seven registries, and what breaks when one is missed. |
| `skills/skillfactory/references/evals.md` | What makes a baseline real instead of decorative. |
| `skills/skillfactory/references/readme.md` | The README house style every skill here follows. |
| `skills/skillfactory/evals/` | A real `scaffold` run of the `repocount` demo spec, re-run and byte-compared. |

## Quick start

```bash
skillfactory detect                                   # every registry, as one table
skillfactory check-spec --spec repocount.spec.json        # graded harder than CI, while it is still free
skillfactory scaffold  --spec repocount.spec.json         # the tree + all seven wiring points
skillfactory freeze --skill repocount --from ./run --command "…" --trap-command "…"
skillfactory verify --skill repocount                     # the ladder, and which rung you reached
```

Install from the [claude-skills marketplace](https://github.com/natejswenson/claude-skills),
then describe the skill you want.

## Triggers

- "create a skill"
- "new skill"
- "make me a skill that"
- "scaffold a skill"
- "add a skill to the marketplace"
- Turning an idea into a versioned, tested, installable skill.

## Requirements

- Node 18+ for the CLI itself.
- Python 3.12 to run the house lints at rung 1 (`score_skill.py`,
  `lint_plugin.py`, `lint_baseline.py`).
- `press` and `ghfactory` for the brand and workflow steps. Both ship in this repo.

## The ladder

| Rung | Proves | How |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | wiring resolves — marketplace, plugin.json, required check, press target, caller, README | `skillfactory verify` |
| 1 | house lints pass | `skillfactory verify` |
| 2 | the skill's own tests pass | `npm test` in the skill |
| **3** | **a real run is frozen as the baseline** | `skillfactory freeze` |
| 4 | CI green on the `feature/* → dev` PR | GitHub |
| 5 | released — the tag is cut | version bump + promotion |

Rungs 0–2 mean the scaffolding is correct, which is not the same as the skill
working. **Never call a skill done below rung 3.**

## Two things skillfactory writes but cannot apply

- `.github/repo-settings.sh` only takes effect when an admin runs it. Editing the
  contexts array changes a file, not GitHub.
- The baseline row in `CLAUDE.md`'s eval table is prose, and what a baseline
  catches is a judgment about failure modes rather than a template.

## Development

```bash
cd skills/skillfactory/skills/skillfactory
npm test
```

Node skill. `ci / skillfactory` runs the same tests plus the house lints on every pull
request; `ci / marketplace` runs `skillfactory verify --all` unconditionally, so a
conformance regression in any skill fails the PR that causes it.
